pl-l4d32c3-d1e115.summary: States that though the debt must always be rendered to one asking, it is not lawful to ask on any day.
claims: Asking for the debt is restricted by times.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine: a Christian may sometimes unite with his wife and sometimes not; on days of procession and fasting it is not lawful, since one should abstain even from lawful things to obtain more easily what is asked.
claims: Spouses should abstain on days of procession and fasting.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e127.summary: Adds Augustine: whenever Christmas or other feasts come, abstain not only from concubines but from your own wives.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e134.summary: Adds Ambrose: if a wife is taken for procreation, not much time seems granted for its use, since feast days, days of procession, and the course of conception and childbirth according to the law show that use of the flesh should cease at those times.
claims: Feasts, processions, conception, and childbirth call for abstinence.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e143.summary: Objects with Jerome against the claim that rendering the debt is not sin: whoever renders his wife the debt cannot devote himself to prayer or eat the Lamb's flesh.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e152.summary: Adds Jerome: if those who had touched their wives could not eat the showbread, how much less may the bread from heaven be violated by those who were just in conjugal embraces; not that we condemn marriage, but at the time we eat the Lamb's flesh we should be free from carnal works.
claims: Those who have just had intercourse should not receive the eucharist.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e161.summary: Interprets this as properly concerning ministers of the Church, who were not permitted to celebrate the sacred offices and mysteries at the time of conjugal embrace, when the Spirit's presence is not given.
claims: Jerome's rule concerns ministers celebrating the mysteries.

pl-l4d32c3-d1e164.summary: Quotes Jerome: lawful marriages are without sin, yet at the time conjugal acts are done the presence of the Holy Spirit will not be given, even if he who performs the work of generation seems a prophet.
claims: Lawful marriage is without sin, but the Spirit's presence is withheld during the act.

pl-l4d32c3.summary: Though the debt must always be rendered when asked, it may not be asked on any day: Augustine and Ambrose call for abstaining on days of processions, fasts, Christmas and other feasts, and during conception and childbirth. Jerome's saying that one who renders the debt cannot pray or eat the Lamb's flesh, and that those who had embraced their wives could not eat the showbread, seems to contradict that rendering is no sin; Lombard refers it properly to ministers of the Church, who may not celebrate the sacred mysteries at the time of conjugal union, when the Spirit's presence is not given, though lawful marriage is without sin.
claims: The marital debt must be rendered, but asking for it on holy days is wrong.
Abstinence is required on feasts, fasts, and processions.
Ministers may not celebrate the mysteries at the time of conjugal union.
